title: Manitoba chiefs call for probe of shooting
article: The Assembly of Manitoba Chiefs is calling for an independent investigation into the fatal police shooting earlier this week of a man wanted on a Canada-wide warrant.
Donald Miles, 34, was shot twice in the stomach during a standoff with four police officers outside a service station Monday night.

"I believe that in order for the Winnipeg Police Service to maintain public confidence and the appearance of propriety, the police chief must submit to an outside agency," AMC Grand Chief Dennis White Bird said Thursday.
Witnesses said the knife-wielding Miles lunged at an officer.

An unidentified police source quoted by the Winnipeg Sun said Miles was an associate of the Manitoba Warriors, an aboriginal street gang, before he recently went to prison for a long list of offences, including assaulting a police officer.
Miles, who was wanted for parole violation, bled to death from gunshot wounds.
One of the officers suffered a wound to his left thigh from what is believed to be a ricocheted bullet.
